In [[homological algebra]], the '''Cartan–Eilenberg resolution''' is in a sense, a [[Resolution (algebra)|resolution]] of a [[chain complex]]. It can be used to construct [[#Hyper-derived functors|hyper-derived functors]]. It is named in honor of [[Henri Cartan]] and [[Samuel Eilenberg]].

== Definition ==
Let <math>\mathcal{A}</math> be an [[Abelian category]] with [[enough projectives]], and let <math>A_{*}</math> be a chain complex with objects in <math>\mathcal{A}</math>. Then a '''Cartan–Eilenberg resolution''' of <math>A_{*}</math> is an upper half-plane [[double complex]] <math>P_{*,*}</math> (i.e., <math>P_{p,q} = 0</math> for <math>q < 0</math>) consisting of projective objects of <math>\mathcal{A}</math> and an "augmentation" chain map <math>\varepsilon \colon P_{p,*} \to A_p</math> such that

* If <math>A_{p} = 0 </math> then the ''p''-th column is zero, i.e. <math>P_{p, q} = 0</math> for all ''q''.

* For any fixed column <math>P_{p, *}</math>,
** The complex of boundaries <math>B_p(P, d^h) := d^h(P_{p+1. *})</math> obtained by applying the horizontal differential to <math>P_{p+1, *}</math> (the <math>p+1</math>st column of <math>P_{*,*}</math>) forms a projective resolution <math>B_p(\varepsilon): B_p(P, d^h) \to B_p(A)</math> of the boundaries of <math>A_p</math>.
** The complex <math>H_p(P, d^h)</math> obtained by taking the homology of each row with respect to the horizontal differential forms a projective resolution <math>H_p(\varepsilon): H_p(P, d^h) \to H_p(A)</math> of degree ''p'' homology of <math>A</math>.

It can be shown that for each ''p'', the column <math>P_{p, *}</math> is a projective resolution of <math>A_{p}</math>.

There is an analogous definition using injective resolutions and cochain complexes.

The existence of Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions can be proved via the [[horseshoe lemma]].

=== Hyper-derived functors ===

Given a right [[exact functor]] <math>F \colon \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}</math>, one can define the left hyper-derived functors of <math>F</math> on a chain complex <math>A_{*}</math> by 

* Constructing a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution <math>\varepsilon: P_{*, *} \to A_{*}</math>, 
* Applying the functor <math>F</math> to <math>P_{*, *}</math>, and 
* Taking the homology of the resulting total complex.

Similarly, one can also define right hyper-derived functors for left exact functors.
